Pianist and composer Sir Roland Hanna was born in Detroit on February 10, 1932. His early training was in classical music and he studied at Eastman and Juilliard. By the late 1950s his passion for music realized itself in the world of jazz and he began displaying his versatility with a diverse group of band leaders. Roland has recorded frequently with the Thad Jones-Mel Lewis Orchestra, the New York Jazz Quartet and as a leader of his own trio.
Roland Hanna was the guest of honor at the Paradise Valley Jazz Party in Scottsdale, Arizona. He was interviewed there on April 15, 2000, by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.
We are filming in Scottsdale, Arizona at the Paradise Valley Jazz Party. My name is Monk Rowe and I am very, very pleased to have Sir Roland Hanna here as my guest.
It’s my pleasure, Monk. Thank you for inviting me.
Congratulations on this honor you’ve got here.
Oh that’s really something. I never thought that I’d be the guy they’d be honoring. Because I always figured hey, I’m too young for that kind of stuff.
